problems.title: Task 8
problems.statement: Using the starchart **(Fig.1)** answer the following questions:

figures.alt: Star chart of Scorpius and surrounding constellations (Ophiuchus, Serpens Caput, Serpens Cauda, Sagittarius, Libra, Lupus, Ara, Norma) with right ascension 15h–19h and declination 0° to −50° grid lines, the ecliptic drawn as a blue line, stars Antares, Shaula, Lesath, Graffias and Greek-letter stars labelled, NGC 6231 and 6124 marked, four positions marked with letters A, B, C, D, and a magnitude legend 1–6.

parts.statement:
What is the ecliptic latitude of the galactic center?

Answer: $\beta =$ \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ deg

The positions of four objects from the Messier catalog are indicated using Latin letters. Which are these objects?

A: M\_\_\_\_\_\_ B: M\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ C: M\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ D: M\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

solution.statement:
**8.1.** What is the ecliptic latitude of the galactic center?

$\beta = -5.5$ deg *1pt*

**8.2.** The positions of four objects from the Messier catalog are indicated using Latin letters. Which are these objects?

A: M7

B: M6

C: M4

D: M80 *2 pts*

problems.title: Task 9
problems.statement: All eight stars brighter than 2 mag have been erased from the map **(Fig.2).**

figures.alt: Negative photograph of a star field in the winter sky, rotated so that east points up and north points right (arrows labelled E and N in the top right corner); the objects NGC 2237, M42 and α Lep are labelled; the bright stars have been erased.

parts.statement: Fill in their positions and names (e.g. Deneb or α Cyg) back on the map.

Which constellation is exactly in the southwestern (SW) corner of the map? Write its standard three-letter Latin designation.

Answer: \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

solution.statement:
**9.1.** Fill in the positions and names back on the map

![](p9-sol-fig1)

*(0.25 pts for position, 0.25 pts for name, a total of 4 pts for 8 stars)*

**9.2.** Which constellation is exactly in the southwestern (SW) corner of the map? Write its standard three-letter Latin designation.

Eri *(Eridanus)* *1 pt*

figures.alt: The Fig. 2 star field with the erased bright stars restored and labelled: Alhena (γ Gem), Aldebaran (α Tau), Procyon (α CMi), Betelgeuse (α Ori), Bellatrix (γ Ori), Alnilam (ε Ori), Rigel (β Ori), Sirius (α CMa) and Mirzam (β CMa).

problems.title: Task 10
problems.statement: The diagram **(Fig.3)** shows how the altitude of three stars above the horizon changes during a night near the winter solstice as observed from the Rozhen observatory (41°41′N, 24°44′E). The one-digit numbers on the chart are the numbers of the stars, while the two-digit numbers are angular distances from the moon in degrees.

figures.caption: Fig. 3
figures.alt: Altitude versus time diagram (altitude 0°–90° on the left axis, airmass on the right axis, UT and local time on the horizontal axis from 15h to 5h) with sunset at 15h 0m, twilight at 16h33m and 4h 3m, sunrise at 5h35m; three curves marked with star numbers 1, 2, 3 (magenta) and angular distances from the Moon in degrees (blue two-digit numbers); two vertical solid lines near 22 and 24 UT.

parts.statement:
How many days after the preceding new moon is this night?

*Answer:* $t =$ \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ *d*

solution.statement:
**10.1.** What are the equatorial coordinates of the three stars?

*Star 1:* $\alpha = 9h$ $\delta = +79$ *deg*

*Star 2:* $\alpha = 5h$ $\delta = -13$ *deg*

*Star 3:* $\alpha = 10h$ $\delta = +22$ *deg*

*3 pts*

**10.2.** How many days after the preceding new moon is this night?

*Answer:* $t = 20 – 21$ *d* *2 pts*

problems.title: Task 11
problems.statement:
This image of a field around a quasar is obtained with a 35-cm telescope.

![](p11-fig1)

It is one of the following four quasars (on the finder charts on **Fig. 5**):

figures.alt: Black-background image of a star field around a quasar with direction arrows labelled N (up-right) and E (up-left).

figures.caption: Fig. 5
figures.alt: Four finder charts in a 2×2 grid: 3C 66A (field stars marked 130, 220, 100, 340; scale 10′), PKS 1510-08 (field stars marked 160, 270, 180, 280; scale 10′), OJ 287 (field stars marked 170, 310, 160; scale bar 5′) and 3C 454.3 (field stars marked 120, 250, 310, 290; scale bar 1′); each chart has N and E direction marks and the quasar indicated by a cross.

parts.statement:
Which quasar is on the image? Identify the field and circle the correct answer.

*Answer:* *3C 66A / OJ 287 / 3C 454.3 / PKS 1510-08*

What changes have to be made in the equatorial coordinates of the telescope in order to put the quasar in the center of the field?

*Answer:* $\Delta\alpha =$ \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ $''$ $\Delta\delta =$ \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ $''$

Approximate distances to some field stars are indicated on the charts in parsecs. Estimate roughly the distance to the quasar:

*Answer:* $d =$ \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ *pc*

solution.statement:
**11.1.** Which quasar is on the image? Identify the field and circle the correct answer.

*Answer:* *OJ 287* *1 pt*

**11.2.** What changes have to be made in the equatorial coordinates of the telescope in order to put the quasar in the center of the field?

*Answer:* $\Delta\alpha = -91''$ $\Delta\delta = +48''$ *(the signs matter!)* *2 pts*

**11.3.** Approximate distances to some field stars are indicated on the charts in parsecs. Estimate roughly the distance to the quasar:

*0 pts:* $d < 1$ *Mpc or* $d > 15$ *Gpc*

*0.5 pts:* $d = 1 – 99$ *Mpc*

*1 pt:* $d = 100$ *Mpc – 15 Gpc*

*A trick question. The actual quasar is at z=0.306, corresponding to a distance of ~1 Gpc, which cannot be derived from the charts. The nearest active quasar known is at a distance of ~180 Mpc.*

problems.title: Task 12
problems.statement:
The speed of the daily motion of stars due to the rotation of the Earth is artificially increased *(video clip)*. What is the geographical latitude of the location of the observation that the software is simulating? North or south of the equator (underline the correct option)?

*Answer:* \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_*North/South*

solution.statement:
**Task 12.** What is the geographical latitude of the location of the observation that the software is simulating?

*Answer: 32 degrees South* *3 pts*
